hero.headline: Your agent, as an app
hero.sub: The same Claude Code engine, rendered as the app instead of as scrollback — and now the screen every session opens in. What it makes, it shows you, right where you're already looking.

shot.alt: A chat turn showing git log output in a code block and an image the agent embedded inline with a caption underneath
shot.caption: Command output as a code block, and the picture the agent referenced rendered in place.

blocks.title: Questions become buttons
blocks.body: When Claude asks something — a choice, a permission, a survey — it stops being a line of text you have to answer by typing the right thing. It becomes a card with the options on it, and your click is the answer.

shot.alt: A native survey card: the question, four described options with radio buttons, a selected count and a Submit button

blocks.title: Tools show their work
blocks.body: Every tool call is its own card with a one-line description of what it's doing and a live status. Expand one to see the detail; leave them collapsed and the conversation stays a conversation instead of a wall of output.

shot.alt: A chat turn with a Bash tool card labelled with what the command does and a running status

blocks.title: And it is the screen you land in
blocks.body: You don't have to find a beta toggle. Every Claude entry point — ＋ New, ⌘T, side-by-side splits, reopened tabs, and the sessions Sleep or a delegated task spawn for you — opens Chat, including for people who never turned it on.

shot.alt: The Chat screen: a Claude answer in markdown, an AskUserQuestion tool card, and a native survey card with clickable options and a Submit button
shot.caption: A real session in the app: the answer as prose, the question as a card you click.

blocks.title: Nothing was given up to get here

items.title: The same engine
items.text: Skills, sub-agents, slash commands, permission modes, the SessionStart brain preload — a chat session is Claude Code, headless, rendered natively.

items.title: Both ways, one conversation
items.text: Open a terminal tab in Chat, or a chat in the terminal. They share the transcript and the conversation id, so you switch surface without losing the thread.

items.title: Files stay clickable
items.text: Paths the agent mentions open a preview in place. Boards render on a live canvas, video and audio play inline — no hop out to find your own output.

blocks.title: The terminal is still here, one switch away
blocks.body: Settings → Agents → Agent screen. The full embedded Claude Code TUI stays available as Terminal (legacy); it just stops being the thing you land in. Sessions already running keep the surface they started on, and plain shells (⌃`) are unaffected.

shot.alt: Settings → Agents with the Agent screen dropdown set to Chat (default), above the explanation of the two surfaces

blocks.title: And What's New became a release history
blocks.body: One page per version, not one per feature — so the feed answers "what did 0.18 give me?" instead of listing things that happened. Each release leads with its number, carries a title, and is built from real screenshots of the app rather than a diagram of it. Announcements can hold clips now, so a page can show motion as well as stills.

clip.alt: A recording of the What's New page: the current release as a hero card, then the version rail of earlier releases, then one of them opening full screen and scrolling through its story
clip.caption: The current release up top, every release before it on the rail — and any of them one click from the whole page.

blocks.text: A chat-spawned Claude and a terminal-spawned Claude are the same binary — so the app briefs the agent about the surface it landed in. That's why it embeds a board instead of telling you where it saved one. And if you deliberately switch back to Terminal (legacy), it sticks: the one-time move to Chat runs once and never overrides a choice you made yourself.

closer.title: Where it lives
closer.body: The agent overlay — the corner launcher, or your open/close hotkey. Want the raw surface back? Settings → Agents → Agent screen → Terminal (legacy).
